region_scene_page.compact: Southern hip-hop grew from multiple city scenes that were often under-recognized by coastal rap media before becoming central to mainstream rap.
region_scene_page.standard: Southern hip-hop grew from multiple city scenes that were often under-recognized by coastal rap media before becoming central to mainstream rap. OutKast's Player's Ball, Master P's Make 'Em Say Uhh!, Back That Azz Up - Juvenile feat. Mannie Fresh and Lil Wayne, and Three 6 Mafia feat. UGK's Sippin' on Some Syrup give the scene its high-recognition landmarks.
region_scene_page.deep: Southern hip-hop grew from multiple city scenes that were often under-recognized by coastal rap media before becoming central to mainstream rap. The rhythm often feels lower, looser, more bass-driven, and more regionally coded than East Coast boom bap. OutKast's Player's Ball, Master P's Make 'Em Say Uhh!, Back That Azz Up - Juvenile feat. Mannie Fresh and Lil Wayne, and Three 6 Mafia feat. UGK's Sippin' on Some Syrup give the scene its high-recognition landmarks. From there, the examples move from quick recognition toward medium and deeper scene signals.
